command:
set -eo pipefail
export PATH=/opt/conda/bin:$PATH
export TMPDIR=/tmp HOME=/tmp LC_ALL=C
cd /tmp
echo "== verify the staged genome set against its pinned sha256 =="
printf '%s  %s\n' 6fa8884c45af0178a24c28413ccfdf7018915e843f106667787f749b4a7aaadc genomes20.tar > pins.sha256
sha256sum -c pins.sha256
tar -xf genomes20.tar

echo "== sourmash sketch + all-pairs compare: 20 genomes, k=21, scaled=1000 =="
# k=21 MATCHES the k mash used. Comparing a k=31 sketch against a k=21 one would be a
# method difference dressed up as disagreement, which is the trap this check exists to avoid.
T0=$(date +%s)
for g in GCF_*.fna.gz; do
  acc="${g%.fna.gz}"
  sourmash sketch dna -p k=21,scaled=1000 "$g" -o "$acc.sig" --name "$acc" 2>> sketch.log
done
sourmash compare ./*.sig --csv sim.csv 2> compare.log
T1=$(date +%s); WALL=$(( T1 - T0 ))

python3 - <<'PYEOF' > metrics.txt
import csv, math

species = {}
for line in open('labels.tsv'):
    acc, sp = line.split('\t')[0], line.split('\t')[1]
    species[acc] = sp

rows = list(csv.reader(open('sim.csv')))
names = [n.strip() for n in rows[0]]
sim = {}
for i, r in enumerate(rows[1:]):
    for j, v in enumerate(r):
        sim[(names[i], names[j])] = float(v)

n = len(names)
diag_min = min(sim[(a, a)] for a in names)
diag_max = max(sim[(a, a)] for a in names)

# Nearest neighbour by similarity, against the same NCBI-derived truth mash was checked on.
nn_ok = 0
for a in names:
    best = max((b for b in names if b != a), key=lambda b: sim[(a, b)])
    if species[a] == species[best]:
        nn_ok += 1

within = [sim[(a, b)] for a in names for b in names
          if a < b and species[a] == species[b]]
between = [sim[(a, b)] for a in names for b in names
           if a < b and species[a] != species[b]]

# mash distance for the same unordered pairs. mash and sourmash estimate the same k-mer
# overlap but with different MinHash variants (bottom-s vs FracMinHash), which disagree
# systematically when genome sizes differ -- so the comparable question is RANK, not value.
mash = {}
for line in open('dist.tsv'):
    f = line.split('\t')
    a, b = f[0].replace('.fna.gz', ''), f[1].replace('.fna.gz', '')
    mash[(a, b)] = float(f[2])

pairs = [(a, b) for a in names for b in names if a < b]

def rank(v):
    order = sorted(range(len(v)), key=lambda i: v[i])
    r = [0.0] * len(v)
    i = 0
    while i < len(order):
        j = i
        while j + 1 < len(order) and v[order[j + 1]] == v[order[i]]:
            j += 1
        avg = (i + j) / 2.0 + 1
        for k in range(i, j + 1):
            r[order[k]] = avg
        i = j + 1
    return r

def spearman(ps):
    xs, ys = [sim[q] for q in ps], [mash[q] for q in ps]
    rx, ry = rank(xs), rank(ys)
    mx, my = sum(rx) / len(rx), sum(ry) / len(ry)
    num = sum((a - mx) * (b - my) for a, b in zip(rx, ry))
    den = math.sqrt(sum((a - mx) ** 2 for a in rx) * sum((b - my) ** 2 for b in ry))
    return num / den if den else float("nan")

# Measured: 123 of the 190 pairs have sourmash similarity EXACTLY 0 (no shared hashes at
# k=21/scaled=1000), and on the mash side those same 123 take only 5 distinct values, up in
# mash's saturation region. Both tools are saying "no detectable relationship" -- that is
# agreement expressed as ties, and ties on both sides cap any rank statistic. Including them
# gives -0.9048, which measures the tie structure rather than the tools. So the comparison is
# restricted to pairs where both have signal, and reported separately for the within-species
# pairs, which are the ones anyone actually needs ranked.
signal = [q for q in pairs if sim[q] > 0.0]
within_pairs = [q for q in pairs if species[q[0]] == species[q[1]]]
rho_all, rho_signal, rho_within = spearman(pairs), spearman(signal), spearman(within_pairs)

print("signatures %d" % n)
print("diag_min %.6f" % diag_min)
print("diag_max %.6f" % diag_max)
print("nn_ok %d" % nn_ok)
print("min_within %.6f" % min(within))
print("max_between %.6f" % max(between))
print("pairs %d" % len(pairs))
print("signal_pairs %d" % len(signal))
print("spearman_all %.4f" % rho_all)
print("spearman_signal %.4f" % rho_signal)
print("spearman_within %.4f" % rho_within)
PYEOF
cat metrics.txt
V(){ awk -v k="$1" '$1==k{print $2}' metrics.txt; }
SIGS=$(V signatures); DMIN=$(V diag_min); DMAX=$(V diag_max); NN=$(V nn_ok)
WMIN=$(V min_within); BMAX=$(V max_between); PAIRS=$(V pairs); SIG=$(V signal_pairs)
RALL=$(V spearman_all); RSIG=$(V spearman_signal); RWIT=$(V spearman_within)

{
  echo "signatures          $SIGS   want exactly 20"
  echo "self_similarity     $DMIN..$DMAX   want exactly 1 (a genome equals itself)"
  echo "nearest_same_sp     $NN   want exactly 20 of 20   (same NCBI truth mash was checked on)"
  echo "min_within_species  $WMIN"
  echo "max_between_species $BMAX   want < min_within_species   [clean separation]"
  echo "pairs_compared      $PAIRS   want exactly 190"
  echo "pairs_with_signal   $SIG   (sourmash similarity > 0)"
  echo "spearman_all_pairs  $RALL   OBSERVATION ONLY -- capped by ties, not the check"
  echo "spearman_signal     $RSIG   want <= -0.95   [rank agreement where both tools see signal]"
  echo "spearman_within_sp  $RWIT   want exactly -1 (no inversions on the 10 same-species pairs)"
  echo "wall_s              $WALL"
} > smoke-check.txt
cat smoke-check.txt
test "$SIGS"  -eq 20
test "$NN"    -eq 20
test "$PAIRS" -eq 190
awk -v a="$DMIN" -v b="$DMAX" 'BEGIN{exit !(a==1 && b==1)}'
awk -v w="$WMIN" -v b="$BMAX" 'BEGIN{exit !(b<w)}'
awk -v r="$RSIG" 'BEGIN{exit !(r<=-0.95)}'
awk -v r="$RWIT" 'BEGIN{exit !(r==-1)}'
echo "SMOKE CHECK PASSED"
